title: Steel wire common nails: penny size to length and shank diameter

citation.standard: Federal Specification FF-N-105B, Nails, Brads, Staples and Spikes: Wire, Cut and Wrought (17 March 1971)
citation.publisher: General Services Administration, United States of America — a U.S. Government federal specification, in the public domain
citation.where: §3.6.11.2, "Type II, style 10 - Common nails. Steel wire, flat head, diamond point, round smooth shank", page 11, whose table gives S (the penny-size trade designation), L (length, in), D (shank diameter, in) and H (head diameter, in). NOTE ON THE DOCUMENT'S STATUS: FF-N-105B was cancelled on 3 December 1996 (Notice 2) and ASTM F1667, Standard Specification for Driven Fasteners: Nails, Spikes, and Staples, is its successor. F1667's dimension tables are behind a paywall and were not read in the task that wrote this table, so the penny-size-to-length convention here is cited to the last readable primary source that states it in full rather than to F1667. A reviewer with access to F1667 should check these rows against it. HOW TO OPEN THE URL: everyspec serves the PDF only with a Referer, so reach it from the document's own page at http://everyspec.com/FED_SPECS/F/FF-N-105B_9866/ rather than by pasting the file URL, which returns 403.
